    As of April 8, 2026, Iran has agreed to a conditional, two-week ceasefire with the U.S., which includes allowing ships to pass through the Strait of Hormuz after weeks of closure
    . The reopening is part of a deal following threats of massive U.S. strikes. Safe passage is now coordinated with Iran's military. 
    Key details: 
    • Controlled Reopening: Iran's Foreign Minister stated that safe passage is possible, but only via coordination with Iran's Armed Forces and based on "technical limitations".
    • Negotiations: The 10-point proposal to end the conflict is for two weeks, with negotiations for a long-term solution starting soon.
    • Previous Status: Prior to this agreement, Iran had effectively blocked traffic through the crucial waterway for over a month.
    • Context: The decision followed a 5 PM deadline set by President Trump, threatening severe retaliation against Iran.
